A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUMOF work, with readable and matchable text, equations, figures and tables. V1 ends after its references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes Appendices A-M. Supplementary additions are assessed as newly documented in the supplied PDFs, without assuming when experiments were performed.

before.justification: V1 reports original HUMOF forecasting results on four datasets and component ablations in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and reports additional sensitivity, robustness, interpretability, long-term forecasting and physical-penetration evaluations in its appendices.

M1.justification: The default HUMOF architecture, DCT rescaling, inference procedure and loss remain unchanged. Appendix L adds an implemented SE(3) interaction-encoding variant using body-local coordinate frames, 6D rotations and relative translation. This is a limited experimental variant.

E1.justification: The four core datasets are retained. V3 substantially expands tested scenarios to missing people and scene points, noisy inputs, interactions within 15 cm, moving objects and 10-second forecasting (Appendices D, G, H and M). These introduce distinct input conditions and forecasting requirements.

E2.justification: The forecasting comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged. V3 adds a random-chance comparator for attention-based interaction-object identification on HUMANISE: Table 9 reports 10.56% accuracy against HUMOF's 83.85%.

E3.justification: V3 adds NPSS, FID, penetration and object-identification evaluations, alongside long-horizon and input-corruption protocols and upsampling of rare moving-object examples. Appendix A also changes the reported HIK setting from 30 observed/60 predicted frames to 25/50. This is an explicit protocol-description revision, although the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v3 adds injection-schedule, point-count, Transformer-depth and SE(3) analyses; occlusion and noise robustness; attention interpretability; close-interaction and penetration analyses; and illustrated failure cases. These substantially expand the questions tested about effectiveness, robustness and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability or significance tests. The added NPSS and FID evaluations are motion-quality metrics, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 376 numerical entries in the original benchmark and ablation tables are retained. V3 adds substantial results, including 10-second path/pose errors of 747.8/188.7 mm and moving-object subset errors of 244.8/159.4 mm. Table 14 additionally finds MutualDistance best on human-to-scene penetration and HUMOF best on human-to-human penetration. These are new evaluations, not improvements to the retained scores.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds explicit mathematical definitions of penetration depth through summed negative-SDF magnitudes and penetration rate through the fraction of penetrating joints, followed by frame/sample averaging. The original model equations and loss are retained, with the loss relocated to Appendix A; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: hierarchical human-human/human-scene representations, coarse-to-fine spatial and frequency reasoning, and state-of-the-art forecasting across four datasets. Changes to dynamic-scene wording do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of attention interpretability, holistic scene representation and close-interaction constraints. Appendices J-K qualify penetration scores and disclose abrupt-motion failures, limitations of distance-based modeling and the absence of explicit future-interaction coupling. Dynamic-object applicability is also discussed with qualifications about scarce training data.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly supplies layer widths, attention-head counts, GCN depth, sigma, dropout, optimizer settings, batch-sampling rules and rotation augmentation. V3 also identifies the FID feature extractor and supplies a planned code-repository location. Most architecture and training additions are newly disclosed details; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations supporting NPSS, T2M-based FID, SE(3) encoding and InterX examples. The main positioning relative to scene-aware, social-aware and SAST approaches remains unchanged. Citation-style changes and expanded bibliographic metadata are presentation edits.

P1.justification: Most introduction, methodology and conclusion prose is retained. V3 shortens the title, revises interaction terminology and author information, moves loss/setup/dataset material into appendices, separates comparisons from discussions, and adds publication statements. These are localized edits and reorganization around a stable main narrative.

P2.justification: V3 merges v1's GTA-IM and HUMANISE tables into Table 2 and renumbers the retained ablation table. It adds Tables 4-16 and Figures 6-10, including robustness plots, additional visual comparisons and failure cases. Colored result highlighting and the ICLR layout also change presentation substantially.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important gaps in v1's robustness validation and reproducibility through extensive supplementary tests and implementation details. Penetration comparisons and explicit failure cases also make the method's capabilities and limitations more assessable. The unreconciled HIK frame specification and continued absence of run-to-run uncertainty remain weaknesses, but the overall evidential and documentation gains are substantial.
